newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IBEC calls for elimination of Irish borrowing.
newsitem.headline: IBEC calls for elimination of Irish borrowing.

text.p: The Irish Business and Employers' Confederation (IBEC) said on Wednesday that healthy exchequer returns should be used to eliminate borrowing.
Figures released on Tuesday showed an Exchequer surplus of 929 million punts at end-July against forecasts of 570 to 600 million.

"It seems likely that the budgetary outturn is heading for a substantial surplus rather than the deficit of 640 million budgeted at the start of the year. This must not be a signal for increased spending or enhanced tax concessions," IBEC said in a statement.
The employers' organisation said upward pressure on spending would only expose the economy to serious financial difficulties in the event of an economic slowdown.
It also noted that the consumption component of the economy was growing strongly and, combined with Irish pound weakness against sterling, could lead to some inflationary push.

"The most sensible action for the Minister for Finance to take, therefore, is to run an exchequer surplus this year...establish a precedent of EBR surpluses over the coming years and make inroads into repaying the high burden of government debt.
"This would enhance the competitiveness and flexibility of the economy which is the best method of ensuring that the fruits of economic growth result in continuing employment growth," IBEC said.
